deploy.description: Notion Agreement Pipeline 'Send to eSignatures' button -> eSignatures.com DRAFT contract whose text is the row's own page body. Document type picks the shell template and signer 1 (Signatory contact or Consultant; Override email wins); Dennis is always signer 2. A resend updates an unsent draft in place. Writes the draft link to 'eSignatures contract', sets Status = Ready to send, and maps the contract (Agreement Type = Agreement) in the eSignatures Mapping Table. Replaces sow-send-for-signing, project-addendum-send-for-signing and notion-nda-to-esignatures-draft (TKT-1088).
deploy.enable_note: Published disabled by the merge of PR #335. Enabled 2026-11-27 with `enable-workflow` so the TKT-1088 end-to-end tests could run. Zapier issued no catch URL while the Zap was disabled: `triggers[0].details` stayed null until enable-workflow, after which `details.webhook_url` appeared at once and the trigger went active.

trigger.trigger_note: Catch hook. The sender is the Agreement Pipeline database's `Send to eSignatures` button property ('Send webhook' action). After the first publish, paste the `webhook_url` readback into that button. `trigger_url` is Zapier-internal and answers an unauthenticated POST with 401 — never point Notion at it.

connection_notes.notion_wf: work.flowers workspace connection. Never the `Knoxx | Dennis #2` connection (02b95b31-c152-8800-9036-1107e08f70da), which cannot see work.flowers databases. Verified 2026-11-27 that it reads Agreement Pipeline after the database moved into the restricted Finance, Legal and HR teamspace.
connection_notes.esign: The PUBLIC `EsignaturesioCLIAPI` app ('eSignatures'), the same connection notion-nda-to-esignatures-draft and esignatures-status-to-notion bind. Every eSignatures call here goes through it: create_contract (template + `placeholder_fields_markdown_map` + two signers + metadata), query_contract, update_contract_placeholder_fields and update_signer. The private `App236843CLIAPI` app the SOW flow used is not needed: it cannot take a second signer.

notion.properties_read: Agreement Name (title), Document type (select), Status (status), Signatory (relation to Contacts), Signer name / Signer email (rollups via Signatory), Override email (email), Consultant (people), Parent agreement (relation), Counterparty (rich_text, registered legal name), eSignatures contract (url) — plus the page BODY via GET /v1/pages/{id}/markdown, which is the contract text. Names checked against the live schema 2026-11-27.
notion.properties_written: eSignatures contract (url) = the draft link, which contains the contract id; Status = "Ready to send". Nothing else: "Sent for signature" and "Signed" belong to esignatures-status-to-notion.
notion.template_mode_note: Repo rule 5 does not apply — this workflow only updates an existing page.

esignatures.template_note: Read back 2026-11-27 with query_template / query_template_content: Scope of Work and Consultant Project Addendum are exactly `{{contract-body}}`; Mutual NDA is `{{ contract-body }}`, a page break, and a Signatory Details section with the required every-signer `signatory_title` field. No template was changed.
esignatures.action_note: `save_as_draft: "yes"`, `test: "no"`, `metadata` = the Notion page id, `assigned_user_email` = Dennis. create_contract runs with maxAttempts 1: it is not idempotent.

tables.01KHZEP4FA560E9GMTGTBR1E2N: eSignatures Mapping — read by Page ID before the eSignatures check (covers a link cleared by hand), then written after the Notion write-back: find by Page ID, update or create, with Page ID, Contract ID and Agreement Type = "Agreement" (exact string, the TKT-1089 contract). Read by esignatures-status-to-notion. Table ops cost no tasks.
